handback.title: Hotfix issues build from their text and get reviewed
handback.summary: An issue labeled hotfix is built from its own text, then code-reviewed and gated, with no plan.
handback.user_story: A small fix labeled hotfix is built straight from its text, reviewed and gated, with no plan.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a code owner says work on an issue labeled hotfix, the worker starts with no plan.
acceptance_criteria.words: By hand, the owner's `/work` starts a hotfix's worker.

edge_cases.case: An issue without the label and with no plan still starts no worker.

acceptance_criteria.text: When an issue labeled hotfix has no open blocker on autopilot, its worker starts instead of its planner.
acceptance_criteria.words: When its turn comes (by hand, or on autopilot once nothing open blocks it), the worker builds straight from the issue's text

edge_cases.case: A hotfix still blocked by an open issue starts nothing.
A sibling without the label still starts its planner.
Switching autopilot on starts an unblocked hotfix's worker.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker starts, its pack gives the issue's text as the whole ask, with no plan.
acceptance_criteria.words: the worker builds straight from the issue's text: the text is the whole ask.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The ask is the issue's text as written; the owner named no other case.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker changes a code file or a test, the change stays on the pull request.
acceptance_criteria.words: The worker may add or change a small test that pins the fix

edge_cases.case: A new code file the worker adds stays too.
An older test the worker changes stays changed.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix worker finishes, code review starts on its pull request.
acceptance_criteria.words: Code review still runs and judges the diff against the issue's text
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Opening the pull request and starting review have no case the owner named.

acceptance_criteria.text: When code review judges a hotfix, its pack gives the issue's text as the ask to judge against.
acceptance_criteria.words: judges the diff against the issue's text; it is the judgment gate.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The review reads the same issue text as the worker; the owner named no other case.

acceptance_criteria.text: When code review approves a hotfix pull request whose checks pass, its merge gate passes, as for any pull request.
acceptance_criteria.words: All tests and the merge gate still run, as for any pull request.

edge_cases.case: A Dokima pull request with no plan and no label still fails its check.
An approved hotfix whose required check fails does not pass the gate.

acceptance_criteria.text: When code review finds a hotfix change bigger than the ask, the planner starts on the issue.
acceptance_criteria.words: When code review finds the change bigger than the ask

edge_cases.case: Once planned again, the worker builds the approved plan.

acceptance_criteria.text: When code review sends a hotfix back to planning, the issue gets a comment saying why.
acceptance_criteria.words: it goes back to normal planning, saying why.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: One comment naming the reviewer's reason; the owner named no other case.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a hotfix's worker or code review starts, its prompt names nothing from Dokima's own repo.
acceptance_criteria.words: keep the prompts free of anything about Dokima's own repo, so they fit any repo.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The owner named no other case; both prompts are checked in one run each.
